public_rationale: CRS stated on October 23, 2026 that the DeepSeek restrictions limit federal procurement but do not restrict nongovernmental access or use [e1]. That evidence does not establish a general US ban on Chinese AI models or measure consumer prices and innovation under such a ban, so the conditional forecast remains unresolved [e1].
limitations: The packet does not establish a general ban; it does not prove the absence of every relevant restriction.
No qualifying causal evaluation of consumer prices or innovation is provided.
Effects of federal procurement restrictions cannot establish the effects of a general ban.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Banning Chinese AI models would raise consumer prices and stifle innovation.
conditions: if the US bans Chinese models

statement.excerpt: Variant on the above; sure to raise prices to consumers, and stifle innovation.
statement.document_title: China has all but caught up. The US is not going to “win” the AI war. Here’s what we should do instead.

from_speaker: sure to raise prices to consumers
our_interpretation: Altogether means an implemented general US prohibition on Chinese AI models, including ordinary commercial and consumer use. A restriction on federal agencies or one vendor alone does not establish that condition.
Consumer prices means prices paid by US end users for comparable AI services.
Stifle innovation means a material reduction in new products, model improvements, or market entry caused by the ban.
Both effects are evaluated against what would have happened without the ban.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying general ban takes effect and credible causal evidence establishes both higher consumer prices and reduced innovation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete evaluation of a qualifying ban establishes that consumer prices did not rise because of it or that innovation was not suppressed. Brief post-ban observations alone are insufficient.

evidence.locator: Considerations for Congress, paragraph beginning “The FASC limits federal procurement”
evidence.publisher: Congressional Research Service, reproduced by EveryCRSReport.com
evidence.explanation: The documented federal restriction does not establish the forecast's antecedent of banning Chinese models altogether. It supplies no outcome evidence about consumer prices or innovation under such a ban.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Official records establishing an implemented general US ban covering ordinary commercial and consumer use, followed by a sufficiently complete causal evaluation against a credible no-ban comparison. Evidence must establish both higher comparable-service consumer prices and reduced innovation, or establish that at least one of those effects did not occur.
